tweets.text:
it is so tough, but teams/individuals need to normalize "being idle"

Of course, no one ever does nothing. There's always odds/ends to do. But you need to shift away from the idea that everyone needs a "big important project" all the time

When you do that, work can really flow

... part of why this is tough is that we all crave doing impactful work. People get nervous when they are just pottering around. Managers get nervous people will leave. The idea that you might spend a day just fixing some annoying stuff that ISN'T THE MOST IMPORTANT THING is hard

I mean think of things like sprinting perpetually into the sunset. The monotony. The "filling" of time-boxes. The scrutinized quarter plan resembling a Tetris board with the poor "shared teams" pushed to the brink.

All in the spirit of keeping busy

as if we can't keep busy
